findings.body:
**Hard-coded SMTP password in source.** `os.environ.get("SMTP_PASSWORD", "smtp-prod-backup-77")` embeds a credential as the default when the env var is missing. Anyone with repo access can log in as `notifications` on `smtp.internal.example`, and cron jobs without the secret mounted will silently authenticate with this fallback instead of failing closed.

Require the secret (or skip send and log when absent). If `smtp-prod-backup-77` was ever a real password, rotate it immediately.

```suggestion
        password = os.environ.get("SMTP_PASSWORD")
        if not password:
            raise RuntimeError("SMTP_PASSWORD is not set")
        s.login("notifications", password)
```

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change embeds a live-looking SMTP credential in source as a default login password.

## Narrative

`mailer.py` previously required `SMTP_PASSWORD` from the environment (`os.environ["SMTP_PASSWORD"]`), so a missing secret failed closed at login. The PR replaces that with `os.environ.get("SMTP_PASSWORD", "smtp-prod-backup-77")`.

That default is a hard-coded credential in the repository. Anyone with read access to the tree or git history can authenticate as `notifications` against `smtp.internal.example`. Cron environments that omit the secret will silently use the baked-in password instead of failing closed, so misconfiguration becomes credential use rather than a loud crash.

The crash the PR aims to stop is the correct failure mode when the secret is not mounted. Fix configuration/secret mounting for cron (or skip send when the password is absent and log clearly). Rotate any password that matches this string if it was ever real.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
